title: "Chapter 10. Splice-Aware and Genotype Modules"
---

<!-- Generated from wiki/ by scripts/build_user_guide.R. Edit the wiki page, not this file. -->


Two optional modules extend Decant to RNA velocity data and to experiments
that pool cells from genetically different donors.

## 10.1 Splice-aware correction for RNA velocity

RNA velocity uses spliced and unspliced counts separately. The soup has its
own spliced/unspliced composition, which can differ from that of the cells.
In single-nucleus data, for example, the soup is often richer in spliced
cytoplasmic mRNA than the nuclei are. Correcting total counts and then
splitting them by each cell's own ratio would distort velocity, so Decant
corrects each layer with the soup of that layer, measured in the empty
droplets.

```r
library(Decant)
mm  <- simulate_multimodal(seed = 1)
emp_u <- lapply(mm$empties, `[[`, "unspliced")
emp_s <- lapply(mm$empties, `[[`, "spliced")
emp_t <- Map(`+`, emp_u, emp_s)

res <- decant(mm$obs_total, emp_t, sample_of = mm$sample_of, clusters = mm$labels,
              obs_unspliced = mm$obs_unspliced, obs_spliced = mm$obs_spliced,
              empties_unspliced = emp_u, empties_spliced = emp_s)
res$modules
#> [1] "hierarchical_ambient"    "cluster_rho"
#> [3] "splice_aware_correction"
```

- `emp_u` and `emp_s` are the unspliced and spliced counts of the empty
  droplets, one matrix per sample; `emp_t` is their sum.
- Supplying all four layer arguments switches on splice-aware correction.
- rho is still estimated on total counts.
- The result gains `res$corrected_unspliced` and `res$corrected_spliced`;
  `res$corrected` is their sum. Each layer keeps the guarantee that no count
  increases.

To use the corrected layers with velocity tools, replace the spliced and
unspliced layers of your velocity object with these two matrices.

## 10.2 Genotype-based contamination estimates

When cells from several donors are pooled in one channel, each cell's own
alleles are known after demultiplexing (for example with Vireo or
souporcell). Reads carrying another donor's allele at a SNP must be ambient.
This gives a contamination estimate that does not depend on gene expression
at all.

```r
al <- simulate_allelic(seed = 1)
rho_al <- estimate_rho_allelic(al)
round(c(correlation = cor(rho_al, al$rho_true),
        mean_estimated = mean(rho_al), mean_true = mean(al$rho_true)), 3)
#>    correlation mean_estimated      mean_true
#>          0.982          0.199          0.200
```

- `simulate_allelic()` simulates 1,500 cells from 8 donors with known
  contamination.
- The input is a list with four elements:

| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| `own` | Per cell, reads carrying the cell's own allele at informative SNPs |
| `other` | Per cell, reads carrying another donor's allele |
| `donor` | Donor of each cell |
| `abund` | Share of each donor in the pool |

- `estimate_rho_allelic()` converts the share of foreign-allele reads into
  rho, accounting for the fact that part of the soup comes from the cell's
  own donor.

To use it in a full run, pass the same list to `decant()`:

```r
# Requires your own data
res <- decant(cells, empties, clusters = clusters, allelic = my_allele_counts)
```

- `allelic` replaces the expression-based estimate of rho; the soup and the
  correction are unchanged.
